ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in parallelogram $ABCD$, points $E$ and $F$ are on sides $BC$ and $AD$ respectively, with $BE=DF$, $\angle AEC=90^\circ$. Quadrilateral $AECF$ is a rectangle; $BF$ is drawn, and if $AB=4$, $\angle ABC=60^\circ$, and $BF$ bisects $\angle ABC$, what is the length of $AD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the construction, $BF$ bisects $\angle ABC$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABF = \angle FBC$,\\
$\because BC \parallel AD$,\\
$\therefore \angle AFB = \angle FBC$,\\
$\therefore \angle AFB = \angle ABF$,\\
$\therefore AF = AB = 4$,\\
In $\triangle ABE$,\\
$\angle AEB = 90^\circ$, $\angle ABE = 60^\circ$, $AB = 4$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAE = 30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore BE = 2$,\\
$\therefore FD = BE = 2$,\\
$\therefore AD = AF + FD = \boxed{6}$.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/trigonometric route. From the image, place B at (0,0), take BC as the positive x-axis, and take AD parallel to it horizontally. From the text, AB=4 and angle ABC=60°, so vector BA has length 4 and makes a 60° angle with the positive x-axis; hence u=4cos60°=2 and v=4sin60°=2√3. Because BF bisects angle ABC, BF makes a 30° angle with BC, so the slope of BF is tan30°=1/√3. But BF goes from B=(0,0) to F=(L,v), so v/L=1/√3. Therefore L=v√3=(2√3)(√3)=6. Since L=AD, AD=6.
